correctness.rationale: A nilpotent rank-k partial injection is a disjoint union of directed chains, so index k+1 iff all k edges are one chain. Order preservation forces this chain to move monotonically, and the contraction condition becomes weak monotonicity of positive gaps. Such gaps are partitions of span m into k parts; translation yields n-m locations and two distinct orientations. Formal partition generating functions give the exact all-rank Euler product. A uniform Hardy-Ramanujan ratio bound plus a dominated Riemann sum yields E_n/(n p(n)) ->12/pi^2 and the stated constant. Independent brute-force iteration checked every partial injection through n=12 and all rank profiles, plus Euler-product coefficients; finite tests are not used as an infinite proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A partial injection has maximal index if and only if its functional digraph is one directed chain of rank-plus-one vertices. Zero fixed points only asserts acyclicity and permits multiple directed chains, so the rank/fixed-point distributions do not imply the maximal-index stratum. A weakly monotone gap partition is a further metric constraint absent from general partial-injection index results.

value.rationale: The rank-by-maximal-nilpotency-index stratum is a canonical structural invariant in a studied finite transformation monoid, rather than an arbitrary selected subset. The complete classification distinguishes path length from fixed-point counts, translates contraction into the partition lattice, yields a bivariate Euler product for every rank and chain size, and proves a sharp Hardy-Ramanujan-scale asymptotic and exponential rarity relative to the ambient semigroup. The already-known all-nilpotent counts and maximal-rank special case are explicitly excluded from independent novelty.
